capitals.name: Padmavati (Pawaya, near Gwalior)
capitals.note: The page: capital Padmavati, "identified with modern Pawaya near Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh", probably the first Naga seat from Bhima-naga (c. 210-230). The coordinates are approximate (the page gives none); Vidisha may have been the seat before (Vrisha-naga, "possibly ... at Vidisha in the late 2nd century"), and Mathura and Kantipuri (probably Kutwar, Morena) were seats of related branches.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Nagas. The core is Trivedi's reconstruction ("from the Morena and Jhansi districts in the north to Vidisha in the south"); the page gives no area and no map of the early 3rd century, so the radii are the researcher's reading. In Cliopatria this land is the Kushan Empire (97 core cells in 215) and the Western Satraps (146).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the core plus Mathura and Ujjain. The page says the Nagas "later expanded to include Mathura in the north and Ujjain in the south" but dates nothing; 280 is the researcher's bridge between Bhima-naga (c. 210-230) and Bhava-naga (c. 310-335). In Cliopatria, Mathura is Eastern Kushan land only in 238-269 (115 cells of the 100 km disc) and stateless afterwards, and Ujjain is Western Satrap land (124-134 cells).

ledger.note: c. 210: Bhima-naga rules the Nagas from Padmavati after the Kushan decline. "Bhima-naga, r. c. 210-230 CE", probably the first to rule from Padmavati; "The Nagas rose to power after the decline of the Kushan Empire in north-central India, in the early 3rd century." The year is the page's (c.); the extent is Trivedi's reconstruction (Morena and Jhansi to Vidisha).

region.text: Mathura, where the Nagas ruled a second line (the Puranas: "seven" kings at Mathura)

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: the Naga rule extends north to Mathura. "It later expanded to include Mathura in the north"; Trivedi has the Nagas advance toward Kantipuri and Mathura "in the process of invading the Kushan territory", undated, and the page says there is "no concrete evidence" for the Kushan defeat the Bharashiva ashvamedhas are sometimes taken to show. 280 is a bridge, not a date.

region.text: Ujjain, the southern extension ("later expanded to include ... Ujjain in the south")

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: the Naga rule extends south to Ujjain. Coins of the Nagas were found at Ujjain; 280 is a bridge between the first rulers and the reign of Bhava-naga. The Satraps are the counterpart on Cliopatria geometry, not on the page.

ledger.note: c. 347: Samudragupta defeats Ganapati-naga and the Naga lands pass to the Guptas. "The Allahabad Pillar inscription of the Gupta king Samudragupta states that he defeated Ganapati-naga" (Nagas page); the Samudragupta page lists Ganapati-naga and Nagasena among the eight kings of Aryavarta and says their kingdoms "were annexed to the Gupta empire" but gives no date for the campaign. 347 is the gupta-empire dossier's bridge; the Nagas page says only "the mid-4th century".

wars.outcome: Gupta victory: Ganapati-naga and Nagasena among the eight kings of Aryavarta "uprooted"; their kingdoms annexed to the Gupta empire.
wars.note: Undated on the page: it dates the reign only as c. 335-375 (modern scholars put the start between c. 319 and c. 350). 347 is the Gupta dossier's bridged year, used here so that the two dossiers agree.

certainty.note: No border is given by any page; the extent follows coin finds (Pawaya, Narwar, Gohad, Vidisha, Kutwar, Ujjain, Mathura, Jhansi).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks. Two pages opened (budget 2-5): Nagas of Padmavati and Samudragupta. A page on Pawaya/Padmavati, "Bharashiva dynasty" and "Pawaya" did not load as Wikipedia titles (not found), so the capital coordinates are approximate and the Bharashiva identification (Vakataka records: ten ashvamedhas; Rudrasena's mother a daughter of Bhava-naga) is only reported, not drawn. The page gives rulers but only three dates (Bhima-naga c. 210-230, Bhava-naga c. 310-335 on Trivedi's assumption, Ganapati mid-4th century), so no ruler strip. The Mathura and Ujjain extension is undated and recorded at confidence 1 in 280 (a bridge). The sa-02-c report names "Nagas of Vindhyatabi"; the page opened does not treat such a state, so no separate dossier. Gazetteer names needed: Padmavati/Pawaya, Vidisha, Narwar, Kantipuri/Kutwar (all used only in text or capitals).
